NASB.1: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz concerning Judah and Jerusalem, which he saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz [and] Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
NASB.2: Listen, O heavens, and hear, O earth; For the LORD speaks, 'Sons I have reared and brought up, But they have revolted against Me.
NASB.3: 'An ox knows its owner, And a donkey its master's manger, [But] Israel does not know, My people do not understand.'
NASB.4: Alas, sinful nation, People weighed down with iniquity, Offspring of evildoers, Sons who act corruptly! They have abandoned the LORD, They have despised the Holy One of Israel, They have turned away from Him.
NASB.5: Where will you be stricken again, [As] you continue in [your] rebellion? The whole head is sick And the whole heart is faint.
NASB.6: From the sole of the foot even to the head There is nothing sound in it, [Only] bruises, welts and raw wounds, Not pressed out or bandaged, Nor softened with oil.
NASB.7: Your land is desolate, Your cities are burned with fire, Your fields-- strangers are devouring them in your presence; It is desolation, as overthrown by strangers.
NASB.8: The daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, Like a watchman's hut in a cucumber field, like a besieged city.
NASB.9: Unless the LORD of hosts Had left us a few survivors, We would be like Sodom, We would be like Gomorrah.
NASB.10: Hear the word of the LORD, You rulers of Sodom; Give ear to the instruction of our God, You people of Gomorrah.
NASB.11: 'What are your multiplied sacrifices to Me?' Says the LORD. 'I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams And the fat of fed cattle; And I take no pleasure in the blood of bulls, lambs or goats.
NASB.12: 'When you come to appear before Me, Who requires of you this trampling of My courts?
NASB.13: 'Bring your worthless offerings no longer, Incense is an abomination to Me. New moon and sabbath, the calling of assemblies-- I cannot endure iniquity and the solemn assembly.
NASB.14: 'I hate your new moon [festivals] and your appointed feasts, They have become a burden to Me; I am weary of bearing [them].
NASB.15: 'So when you spread out your hands [in prayer], I will hide My eyes from you; Yes, even though you multiply prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are covered with blood.
NASB.16: 'Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean; Remove the evil of your deeds from My sight. Cease to do evil,
NASB.17: Learn to do good; Seek justice, Reprove the ruthless, Defend the orphan, Plead for the widow.
NASB.18: 'Come now, and let us reason together,' Says the LORD, 'Though your sins are as scarlet, They will be as white as snow; Though they are red like crimson, They will be like wool.
NASB.19: 'If you consent and obey, You will eat the best of the land;
NASB.20: 'But if you refuse and rebel, You will be devoured by the sword.' Truly, the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
NASB.21: How the faithful city has become a harlot, She [who] was full of justice! Righteousness once lodged in her, But now murderers.
NASB.22: Your silver has become dross, Your drink diluted with water.
NASB.23: Your rulers are rebels And companions of thieves; Everyone loves a bribe And chases after rewards. They do not defend the orphan, Nor does the widow's plea come before them.
NASB.24: Therefore the Lord GOD of hosts, The Mighty One of Israel, declares, 'Ah, I will be relieved of My adversaries And avenge Myself on My foes.
NASB.25: 'I will also turn My hand against you, And will smelt away your dross as with lye And will remove all your alloy.
NASB.26: 'Then I will restore your judges as at the first, And your counselors as at the beginning; After that you will be called the city of righteousness, A faithful city.'
NASB.27: Zion will be redeemed with justice And her repentant ones with righteousness.
NASB.28: But transgressors and sinners will be crushed together, And those who forsake the LORD will come to an end.
NASB.29: Surely you will be ashamed of the oaks which you have desired, And you will be embarrassed at the gardens which you have chosen.
NASB.30: For you will be like an oak whose leaf fades away Or as a garden that has no water.
NASB.31: The strong man will become tinder, His work also a spark. Thus they shall both burn together And there will be none to quench [them].

ESV.1: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
ESV.2: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth; for the LORD has spoken: “Children  have I reared and brought up, but they have rebelled against me.
ESV.3: The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's crib, but Israel does not know, my people do not understand.”
ESV.4: Ah, sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, offspring of evildoers, children who deal corruptly! They have forsaken the LORD, they have despised the Holy One of Israel, they are utterly estranged.
ESV.5: Why will you still be struck down? Why will you continue to rebel? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.
ESV.6: From the sole of the foot even to the head, there is no soundness in it, but bruises and sores and raw wounds; they are not pressed out or bound up or softened with oil.
ESV.7: Your country lies desolate; your cities are burned with fire; in your very presence foreigners devour your land; it is desolate, as overthrown by foreigners.
ESV.8: And the daughter of Zion is left like a booth in a vineyard, like a lodge in a cucumber field, like a besieged city.
ESV.9: If the LORD of hosts had not left us a few survivors, we should have been like Sodom, and become like Gomorrah.
ESV.10: Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of  Sodom! Give ear to the teaching  of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
ESV.11: “What to me is the multitude of your sacrifices? says the LORD; I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of well-fed beasts; I do not delight in the blood of bulls, or of lambs, or of goats.
ESV.12: “When you come to appear before me, who has required of you this trampling of my courts?
ESV.13: Bring no more vain offerings; incense is an abomination to me. New moon and Sabbath and the calling of convocations — I cannot endure iniquity and solemn assembly.
ESV.14: Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hates; they have become a burden to me; I am weary of bearing them.
ESV.15: When you spread out your hands, I will hide my eyes from you; even though you make many prayers, I will not listen; your hands are full of blood.
ESV.16: Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean; remove the evil of your deeds from before my eyes; cease to do evil,
ESV.17: learn to do good; seek justice, correct oppression; bring justice to the fatherless, plead the widow's cause.
ESV.18: “Come now, let us reason  together, says the LORD: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.
ESV.19: If you are willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land;
ESV.20: but if you refuse and rebel, you shall be eaten by the sword; for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.”
ESV.21: How the faithful city has become a whore,  she who was full of justice! Righteousness lodged in her, but now murderers.
ESV.22: Your silver has become dross, your best wine mixed with water.
ESV.23: Your princes are rebels and companions of thieves. Everyone loves a bribe and runs after gifts. They do not bring justice to the fatherless, and the widow's cause does not come to them.
ESV.24: Therefore the Lord declares, the LORD of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel: “Ah, I will get relief from my enemies and avenge myself on my foes.
ESV.25: I will turn my hand against you and will smelt away your dross as with lye and remove all your alloy.
ESV.26: And I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counselors as at the beginning. Afterward you shall be called the city of righteousness, the faithful city.”
ESV.27: Zion shall be redeemed by justice, and those in her who repent, by righteousness.
ESV.28: But rebels and sinners shall be broken together, and those who forsake the LORD shall be consumed.
ESV.29: For they  shall be ashamed of the oaks that you desired; and you shall blush for the gardens that you have chosen.
ESV.30: For you shall be like an oak whose leaf withers, and like a garden without water.
ESV.31: And the strong shall become tinder, and his work a spark, and both of them shall burn together, with none to quench them.

NKJV.10: Hear the word of the LORD, You rulers of Sodom; Give ear to the law of our God, You people of Gomorrah:
NKJV.11: “To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?” Says the LORD. “I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams And the fat of fed cattle. I do not delight in the blood of bulls, Or of lambs or goats.
NKJV.12: “When you come to appear before Me, Who has required this from your hand, To trample My courts?
NKJV.13: Bring no more futile sacrifices; Incense is an abomination to Me. The New Moons, the Sabbaths, and the calling of assemblies— I cannot endure iniquity and the sacred meeting.
NKJV.14: Your New Moons and your appointed feasts My soul hates; They are a trouble to Me, I am weary of bearing them.
NKJV.15: When you spread out your hands, I will hide My eyes from you;  Even though you make many prayers, I will not hear. Your hands are full of blood.
NKJV.16: “Wash  yourselves, make yourselves clean; Put away the evil of your doings from before My eyes.  Cease to do evil,
NKJV.17: Learn to do good; Seek justice, Rebuke the oppressor; Defend the fatherless, Plead for the widow.
NKJV.18: “Come now, and let us reason together,” Says the LORD, “Though your sins are like scarlet,  They shall be as white as snow; Though they are red like crimson, They shall be as wool.
NKJV.19: If you are willing and obedient, You shall eat the good of the land;
NKJV.20: But if you refuse and rebel, You shall be devoured by the sword”;  For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
NKJV.21: How the faithful city has become a harlot! It was full of justice; Righteousness lodged in it, But now murderers.
NKJV.22: Your silver has become dross, Your wine mixed with water.
NKJV.23: Your princes are rebellious, And companions of thieves; Everyone loves bribes, And follows after rewards. They do not defend the fatherless, Nor does the cause of the widow come before them.
NKJV.24: Therefore the Lord says, The LORD of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, “Ah, I will rid Myself of My adversaries, And take vengeance on My enemies.
NKJV.25: I will turn My hand against you, And thoroughly purge away your dross, And take away all your alloy.
NKJV.26: I will restore your judges as at the first, And your counselors as at the beginning. Afterward you shall be called the city of righteousness, the faithful city.”
NKJV.27: Zion shall be redeemed with justice, And her penitents with righteousness.
NKJV.28: The destruction of transgressors and of sinners shall be together, And those who forsake the LORD shall be consumed.
NKJV.29: For they shall be ashamed of the terebinth trees Which you have desired; And you shall be embarrassed because of the gardens Which you have chosen.
NKJV.30: For you shall be as a terebinth whose leaf fades, And as a garden that has no water.
NKJV.31: The strong shall be as tinder, And the work of it as a spark; Both will burn together, And no one shall quench them.

NLT.1: These are the visions that Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem. He saw these visions during the years when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah.
NLT.2:
Listen, O heavens! Pay attention, earth!
This is what the LORD says:
“The children I raised and cared for
have rebelled against me.
NLT.3:
Even an ox knows its owner,
and a donkey recognizes its master’s care —
but Israel doesn’t know its master.
My people don’t recognize my care for them.”
NLT.4:
Oh, what a sinful nation they are —
loaded down with a burden of guilt.
They are evil people,
corrupt children who have rejected the LORD.
They have despised the Holy One of Israel
and turned their backs on him.
NLT.5:
Why do you continue to invite punishment?
Must you rebel forever?
Your head is injured,
and your heart is sick.
NLT.6:
You are battered from head to foot —
covered with bruises, welts, and infected wounds —
without any soothing ointments or bandages.
NLT.7:
Your country lies in ruins,
and your towns are burned.
Foreigners plunder your fields before your eyes
and destroy everything they see.
NLT.8:
Beautiful Jerusalem stands abandoned
like a watchman’s shelter in a vineyard,
like a lean-to in a cucumber field after the harvest,
like a helpless city under siege.
NLT.9:
If the LORD of Heaven’s Armies
had not spared a few of us,
we would have been wiped out like Sodom,
destroyed like Gomorrah.
NLT.10:
Listen to the LORD, you leaders of “Sodom.”
Listen to the law of our God, people of “Gomorrah.”
NLT.11:
“What makes you think I want all your sacrifices?”
says the LORD.
“I am sick of your burnt offerings of rams
and the fat of fattened cattle.
I get no pleasure from the blood
of bulls and lambs and goats.
NLT.12:
When you come to worship me,
who asked you to parade through my courts with all your ceremony?
NLT.13:
Stop bringing me your meaningless gifts;
the incense of your offerings disgusts me!
As for your celebrations of the new moon and the Sabbath
and your special days for fasting —
they are all sinful and false.
I want no more of your pious meetings.
NLT.14:
I hate your new moon celebrations and your annual festivals.
They are a burden to me. I cannot stand them!
NLT.15:
When you lift up your hands in prayer, I will not look.
Though you offer many prayers, I will not listen,
for your hands are covered with the blood of innocent victims.
NLT.16:
Wash yourselves and be clean!
Get your sins out of my sight.
Give up your evil ways.
NLT.17:
Learn to do good.
Seek justice.
Help the oppressed.
Defend the cause of orphans.
Fight for the rights of widows.
NLT.18:
“Come now, let’s settle this,”
says the LORD.
“Though your sins are like scarlet,
I will make them as white as snow.
Though they are red like crimson,
I will make them as white as wool.
NLT.19:
If you will only obey me,
you will have plenty to eat.
NLT.20:
But if you turn away and refuse to listen,
you will be devoured by the sword of your enemies.

NLT.21:
See how Jerusalem, once so faithful,
has become a prostitute.
Once the home of justice and righteousness,
she is now filled with murderers.
NLT.22:
Once like pure silver,
you have become like worthless slag.
Once so pure,
you are now like watered-down wine.
NLT.23:
Your leaders are rebels,
the companions of thieves.
All of them love bribes
and demand payoffs,
but they refuse to defend the cause of orphans
or fight for the rights of widows.
NLT.24:
Therefore, the Lord, the LORD of Heaven’s Armies,
the Mighty One of Israel, says,
“I will take revenge on my enemies
and pay back my foes!
NLT.25:
I will raise my fist against you.
I will melt you down and skim off your slag.
I will remove all your impurities.
NLT.26:
Then I will give you good judges again
and wise counselors like you used to have.
Then Jerusalem will again be called the Home of Justice
and the Faithful City.”
NLT.27:
Zion will be restored by justice;
those who repent will be revived by righteousness.
NLT.28:
But rebels and sinners will be completely destroyed,
and those who desert the LORD will be consumed.
NLT.29:
You will be ashamed of your idol worship
in groves of sacred oaks.
You will blush because you worshiped
in gardens dedicated to idols.
NLT.30:
You will be like a great tree with withered leaves,
like a garden without water.

and no one will be able to put out the fire.

WEB.1: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
WEB.2: Hear, heavens, and listen, earth; for Yahweh  has spoken: “I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me.
WEB.3: The ox knows his owner, and the donkey his master’s crib; but Israel doesn’t know, my people don’t consider.”
WEB.4: Ah sinful nation, a people loaded with iniquity, offspring  of evildoers, children who deal corruptly! They have forsaken Yahweh. They have despised the Holy One of Israel. They are estranged and backward.
WEB.5: Why should you be beaten more, that you revolt more and more? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.
WEB.6: From the sole of the foot even to the head there is no soundness in it: wounds, welts, and open sores. They haven’t been closed, neither bandaged, neither soothed with oil.
WEB.7: Your country is desolate. Your cities are burned with fire. Strangers devour your land in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.
WEB.8: The daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a field of melons, like a besieged city.
WEB.9: Unless Yahweh of Armies had left to us a very small remnant, we would have been as Sodom; we would have been like Gomorrah.
WEB.10: Hear Yahweh’s word, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the law of our God,  you people of Gomorrah!
WEB.11: “What are the multitude of your sacrifices to me?”, says Yahweh. “I have had enough of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed animals. I don’t delight in the blood of bulls, or of lambs, or of male goats.
WEB.12: When you come to appear before me, who has required this at your hand, to trample my courts?
WEB.13: Bring no more vain offerings. Incense is an abomination to me; new moons, Sabbaths, and convocations: I can’t bear with evil assemblies.
WEB.14: My soul hates your New Moons and your appointed feasts. They are a burden to me. I am weary of bearing them.
WEB.15: When you spread out your hands, I will hide my eyes from you. Yes, when you make many prayers, I will not hear. Your hands are full of blood.
WEB.16: Wash yourselves, make yourself clean. Put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes. Cease to do evil.
WEB.17: Learn to do well. Seek justice. Relieve the oppressed. Judge the fatherless. Plead for the widow.”
WEB.18: “Come now, and let us reason together,” says Yahweh: “Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. Though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
WEB.19: If you are willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land;
WEB.20: but if you refuse and rebel, you shall be devoured with the sword; for the mouth of Yahweh has spoken it.”
WEB.21: How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She was full of justice; righteousness lodged in her, but now murderers.
WEB.22: Your silver has become dross, your wine mixed with water.
WEB.23: Your princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves. Everyone loves bribes, and follows after rewards. They don’t judge the fatherless, neither does the cause of the widow come to them.
WEB.24: Therefore the Lord,  Yahweh of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says: “Ah, I will get relief from my adversaries, and avenge myself on my enemies;
WEB.25: and I will turn my hand on you, thoroughly purge away your dross, and will take away all your tin.
WEB.26: I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counselors as at the beginning. Afterward you shall be called ‘The city of righteousness, a faithful town.’
WEB.27: Zion shall be redeemed with justice, and her converts with righteousness.
WEB.28: But the destruction of transgressors and sinners shall be together, and those who forsake Yahweh shall be consumed.
WEB.29: For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which you have desired, and you shall be confounded for the gardens that you have chosen.
WEB.30: For you shall be as an oak whose leaf fades, and as a garden that has no water.
WEB.31: The strong will be like tinder, and his work like a spark. They will both burn together, and no one will quench them.”

AMP.1: The vision of [the prophet] Isaiah the son of Amoz concerning [the kingdom of] Judah and [its capital] Jerusalem, which he saw [as revealed by God] during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
AMP.2:
Hear, O heavens, and listen, O earth;
For the LORD has spoken:
"I have reared and brought up sons,
But they have rebelled against Me and have broken away.
AMP.3:
"The ox [instinctively] knows its owner,
And the donkey its master's feeding trough,
But Israel does not know [Me as LORD],
My people do not understand."
AMP.4:
Ah, sinful nation,
A people loaded down with wickedness [with sin, with injustice, with wrongdoing],
Offspring of evildoers,
Sons who behave corruptly!
They have abandoned (rejected) the LORD,
They have despised the Holy One of Israel [provoking Him to anger],
They have turned away from Him.
AMP.5:
Why should you be stricken and punished again [since no change results from it]?
You [only] continue to rebel.
The whole head is sick
And the whole heart is faint and sick.
AMP.6:
From the sole of the foot even to the head
There is nothing healthy in the nation's body,
Only bruises, welts, and raw wounds,
Not pressed out or bandaged,
Nor softened with oil [as a remedy].
AMP.7:
Your land lies desolate [because of your disobedience],
Your cities are burned with fire,
Your fields—strangers are devouring them in your very presence;
It is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.
AMP.8:
The Daughter of Zion (Jerusalem) is left like a [deserted] shelter in a vineyard,
Like a watchman's hut in a cucumber field, like a besieged city [isolated, surrounded by devastation].
AMP.9:
If the LORD of hosts
Had not left us a few survivors,
We would be like Sodom,
We would be like Gomorrah.
AMP.10:
Hear the word of the LORD [rulers of Jerusalem],
You rulers of [another] Sodom,
Listen to the law and instruction of our God,
You people of [another] Gomorrah.
AMP.11:
"What are your multiplied sacrifices to Me [without your repentance]?"
Says the LORD.
"I have had enough of [your] burnt offerings of rams
And the fat of well-fed cattle [without your obedience];
And I take no pleasure in the blood of bulls or lambs or goats [offered without repentance].
AMP.12:
"When you come to appear before Me,
Who requires this of you, this trampling of My [temple] courts [by your sinful feet]?
AMP.13:
"Do not bring worthless offerings again,
[Your] incense is repulsive to Me;
[Your] New Moon and Sabbath [observances], the calling of assemblies—
I cannot endure wickedness [your sin, your injustice, your wrongdoing] and [the squalor of] the festive assembly.
AMP.14:
"I hate [the hypocrisy of] your New Moon festivals and your appointed feasts.
They have become a burden to Me;
I am weary of bearing them.
AMP.15:
"So when you spread out your hands [in prayer, pleading for My help],
I will hide My eyes from you;
Yes, even though you offer many prayers,
I will not be listening.
Your hands are full of blood!
AMP.16:
"Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean;
Get your evil deeds out of My sight.
Stop doing evil,
AMP.17:
Learn to do good.
Seek justice,
Rebuke the ruthless,
Defend the fatherless,
Plead for the [rights of the] widow [in court].
AMP.18:
"Come now, and let us reason together,"
Says the LORD.
" Though your sins are like scarlet,
They shall be as white as snow;
Though they are red like crimson,
They shall be like wool.
AMP.19:
"If you are willing and obedient,
You shall eat the best of the land;
AMP.20:
But if you refuse and rebel,
You shall be devoured by the sword."
For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
AMP.21:
How the faithful city has become a prostitute [idolatrous, despicable],
She who was full of justice!
Right standing with God once lodged in her,
But now murderers.
AMP.22:
Your silver has turned to lead,
Your wine is diluted with water.
AMP.23:
Your rulers are rebels
And companions of thieves;
Everyone loves bribes
And chases after gifts.
They do not defend the fatherless,
Nor does the widow's cause come before them [instead they delay or turn a deaf ear].
AMP.24:
Therefore the Lord GOD of hosts,
The Mighty One of Israel, declares:
"Ah, I will be freed of My adversaries
And avenge Myself on My enemies.
AMP.25:
"And I will turn My hand against you,
And will [thoroughly] purge away your dross as with lye
And remove all your tin (impurity).
AMP.26:
"Then I will restore your judges as at the first,
And your counselors as at the beginning;
Afterward you will be called the city of righteousness,
The faithful city."
AMP.27:
Zion will be redeemed with justice
And her repentant ones with righteousness.
AMP.28:
But rebels and sinners will be crushed and destroyed together,
And those who abandon (turn away from) the LORD will be consumed (perish).
AMP.29:
For you will be ashamed [of the degradation] of the oaks in which you took [idolatrous] pleasure,
And you will be ashamed of the gardens [of passion] which you have chosen [for pagan worship].
AMP.30:
For you will be like an oak whose leaf withers and dies
And like a garden that has no water.
AMP.31:
The strong man will become tinder,
And his work a spark.
So both will burn together
And there will be none to quench them.

MSG.1: The vision that Isaiah son of Amoz saw regarding Judah and Jerusalem during the times of the kings of Judah: Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
MSG.2:
Heaven and earth, you're the jury.
Listen to God's case:
"I had children and raised them well,
and they turned on me.
MSG.3:
The ox knows who's boss,
the mule knows the hand that feeds him,
But not Israel.
My people don't know up from down.
MSG.4:
Shame! Misguided God-dropouts,
staggering under their guilt-baggage,
Gang of miscreants,
band of vandals—
My people have walked out on me, their God,
turned their backs on The Holy of Israel,
walked off and never looked back.
MSG.5:
"Why bother even trying to do anything with you
when you just keep to your bullheaded ways?
You keep beating your heads against brick walls.
Everything within you protests against you.
MSG.6:
From the bottom of your feet to the top of your head,
nothing's working right.
Wounds and bruises and running sores—
untended, unwashed, unbandaged.
MSG.7:
Your country is laid waste,
your cities burned down.
Your land is destroyed by outsiders while you watch,
reduced to rubble by barbarians.
MSG.8:
Daughter Zion is deserted—
like a tumbledown shack on a dead-end street,
Like a tarpaper shanty on the wrong side of the tracks,
like a sinking ship abandoned by the rats.
MSG.9:
If God-of-the-Angel-Armies hadn't left us a few survivors,
we'd be as desolate as Sodom, doomed just like Gomorrah.
MSG.10:
"Listen to my Message,
you Sodom-schooled leaders.
Receive God's revelation,
you Gomorrah-schooled people.
MSG.11:
"Why this frenzy of sacrifices?"
God's asking.
"Don't you think I've had my fill of burnt sacrifices,
rams and plump grain-fed calves?
Don't you think I've had my fill
of blood from bulls, lambs, and goats?
MSG.12:
When you come before me,
who ever gave you the idea of acting like this,
Running here and there, doing this and that—
all this sheer commotion in the place provided for worship?
MSG.13:
"Quit your worship charades.
I can't stand your trivial religious games:
Monthly conferences, weekly Sabbaths, special meetings—
meetings, meetings, meetings—I can't stand one more!
MSG.14:
Meetings for this, meetings for that. I hate them!
You've worn me out!
I'm sick of your religion, religion, religion,
while you go right on sinning.
MSG.15:
When you put on your next prayer-performance,
I'll be looking the other way.
No matter how long or loud or often you pray,
I'll not be listening.
And do you know why? Because you've been tearing
people to pieces, and your hands are bloody.
MSG.16:
Go home and wash up.
Clean up your act.
Sweep your lives clean of your evildoings
so I don't have to look at them any longer.
Say no to wrong.
MSG.17:
Learn to do good.
Work for justice.
Help the down-and-out.
Stand up for the homeless.
Go to bat for the defenseless.
MSG.18:
"Come. Sit down. Let's argue this out."
This is God's Message:
"If your sins are blood-red,
they'll be snow-white.
If they're red like crimson,
they'll be like wool.
MSG.19:
If you'll willingly obey,
you'll feast like kings.
MSG.20:
But if you're willful and stubborn,
you'll die like dogs."
That's right. God says so.
MSG.21:
Oh! Can you believe it? The chaste city
has become a whore!
She was once all justice,
everyone living as good neighbors,
And now they're all
at one another's throats.
MSG.22:
Your coins are all counterfeits.
Your wine is watered down.
MSG.23:
Your leaders are turncoats
who keep company with crooks.
They sell themselves to the highest bidder
and grab anything not nailed down.
They never stand up for the homeless,
never stick up for the defenseless.
MSG.24:
This Decree, therefore, of the Master, God-of-the-Angel-Armies,
the Strong One of Israel:
"This is it! I'll get my oppressors off my back.
I'll get back at my enemies.
MSG.25:
I'll give you the back of my hand,
purge the junk from your life, clean you up.
MSG.26:
I'll set honest judges and wise counselors among you
just like it was back in the beginning.
Then you'll be renamed
City-That-Treats-People-Right, the True-Blue City."
MSG.27:
God's right ways will put Zion right again.
God's right actions will restore her penitents.
MSG.28:
But it's curtains for rebels and God-traitors,
a dead end for those who walk out on God.
MSG.29:
"Your dalliances in those oak grove shrines
will leave you looking mighty foolish,
All that fooling around in god and goddess gardens
that you thought was the latest thing.
MSG.30:
You'll end up like an oak tree
with all its leaves falling off,
Like an unwatered garden,
withered and brown.
MSG.31:
'The Big Man' will turn out to be dead bark and twigs,
and his 'work,' the spark that starts the fire
That exposes man and work both
as nothing but cinders and smoke."

my people do not understand.
NRSVCE.4:
Ah, sinful nation,
people laden with iniquity,
offspring who do evil,
children who deal corruptly,
who have forsaken the LORD,
who have despised the Holy One of Israel,
who are utterly estranged!
NRSVCE.5:
Why do you seek further beatings?
Why do you continue to rebel?
The whole head is sick,
and the whole heart faint.
NRSVCE.6:
From the sole of the foot even to the head,
there is no soundness in it,
but bruises and sores
and bleeding wounds;
they have not been drained, or bound up,
or softened with oil.
NRSVCE.7:
Your country lies desolate,
your cities are burned with fire;
in your very presence
aliens devour your land;
it is desolate, as overthrown by foreigners.
NRSVCE.8:
And daughter Zion is left
like a booth in a vineyard,
like a shelter in a cucumber field,
like a besieged city.
NRSVCE.9:
If the LORD of hosts
had not left us a few survivors,
we would have been like Sodom,
and become like Gomorrah.
NRSVCE.10:
Hear the word of the LORD,
you rulers of Sodom!
Listen to the teaching of our God,
you people of Gomorrah!
NRSVCE.11:
What to me is the multitude of your sacrifices?
says the LORD;
I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams
and the fat of fed beasts;
I do not delight in the blood of bulls,
or of lambs, or of goats.
NRSVCE.12:
When you come to appear before me,
who asked this from your hand?
Trample my courts no more;
NRSVCE.13:
bringing offerings is futile;
incense is an abomination to me.
New moon and sabbath and calling of convocation —
I cannot endure solemn assemblies with iniquity.
NRSVCE.14:
Your new moons and your appointed festivals
my soul hates;
they have become a burden to me,
I am weary of bearing them.
NRSVCE.15:
When you stretch out your hands,
I will hide my eyes from you;
even though you make many prayers,
I will not listen;
your hands are full of blood.
NRSVCE.16:
Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean;
remove the evil of your doings
from before my eyes;
cease to do evil,
NRSVCE.17:
learn to do good;
seek justice,
rescue the oppressed,
defend the orphan,
plead for the widow.
NRSVCE.18:
Come now, let us argue it out,
says the LORD:
though your sins are like scarlet,
they shall be like snow;
though they are red like crimson,
they shall become like wool.
NRSVCE.19:
If you are willing and obedient,
you shall eat the good of the land;
NRSVCE.20:
but if you refuse and rebel,
you shall be devoured by the sword;
for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
NRSVCE.21:
How the faithful city
has become a whore!
She that was full of justice,
righteousness lodged in her —
but now murderers!
NRSVCE.22:
Your silver has become dross,
your wine is mixed with water.
NRSVCE.23:
Your princes are rebels
and companions of thieves.
Everyone loves a bribe
and runs after gifts.
They do not defend the orphan,
and the widow’s cause does not come before them.
NRSVCE.24:
Therefore says the Sovereign, the LORD of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel:
Ah, I will pour out my wrath on my enemies,
and avenge myself on my foes!
NRSVCE.25:
I will turn my hand against you;
I will smelt away your dross as with lye
and remove all your alloy.
NRSVCE.26:
And I will restore your judges as at the first,
and your counselors as at the beginning.
Afterward you shall be called the city of righteousness,
the faithful city.
NRSVCE.27:
Zion shall be redeemed by justice,
and those in her who repent, by righteousness.
NRSVCE.28:
But rebels and sinners shall be destroyed together,
and those who forsake the LORD shall be consumed.
NRSVCE.29:
For you shall be ashamed of the oaks
in which you delighted;
and you shall blush for the gardens
that you have chosen.
NRSVCE.30:
For you shall be like an oak
whose leaf withers,
and like a garden without water.
NRSVCE.31:
The strong shall become like tinder,
and their work like a spark;
they and their work shall burn together,
with no one to quench them.

NET.1: Here is the message about Judah and Jerusalem that was revealed to Isaiah son of Amoz during the time when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah reigned over Judah.
NET.2: Listen, O heavens, pay attention, O earth! For the LORD speaks: “I raised children, I brought them up, but they have rebelled against me!
NET.3: An ox recognizes its owner, a donkey recognizes where its owner puts its food; but Israel does not recognize me, my people do not understand.”
NET.4: The sinful nation is as good as dead, the people weighed down by evil deeds. They are offspring who do wrong, children who do wicked things. They have abandoned the LORD, and rejected the Holy One of Israel. They are alienated from him.
NET.5: Why do you insist on being battered? Why do you continue to rebel? Your head has a massive wound, your whole body is weak.
NET.6: From the soles of your feet to your head, there is no spot that is unharmed. There are only bruises, cuts, and open wounds. They have not been cleansed or bandaged, nor have they been treated with olive oil.
NET.7: Your land is devastated, your cities burned with fire. Right before your eyes your crops are being destroyed by foreign invaders. They leave behind devastation and destruction.
NET.8: Daughter Zion is left isolated, like a hut in a vineyard, or a shelter in a cucumber field; she is a besieged city.
NET.9: If the LORD who commands armies had not left us a few survivors, we would have quickly become like Sodom, we would have become like Gomorrah.
NET.10: Listen to the LORD’s word, you leaders of Sodom! Pay attention to our God’s rebuke, people of Gomorrah!
NET.11: “Of what importance to me are your many sacrifices?” says the LORD. “I am stuffed with burnt sacrifices of rams and the fat from steers. The blood of bulls, lambs, and goats I do not want.
NET.12: When you enter my presence, do you actually think I want this — animals trampling on my courtyards?
NET.13: Do not bring any more meaningless offerings; I consider your incense detestable! You observe new moon festivals, Sabbaths, and convocations, but I cannot tolerate sin-stained celebrations!
NET.14: I hate your new moon festivals and assemblies; they are a burden that I am tired of carrying.
NET.15: When you spread out your hands in prayer, I look the other way; when you offer your many prayers, I do not listen, because your hands are covered with blood.
NET.16: Wash! Cleanse yourselves! Remove your sinful deeds from my sight. Stop sinning!
NET.17: Learn to do what is right! Promote justice! Give the oppressed reason to celebrate! Take up the cause of the orphan! Defend the rights of the widow!
NET.18: Come, let’s consider your options,” says the LORD. “Though your sins have stained you like the color red, you can become white like snow; though they are as easy to see as the color scarlet, you can become white like wool.
NET.19: If you have a willing attitude and obey, then you will again eat the good crops of the land.
NET.20: But if you refuse and rebel, you will be devoured by the sword.” Know for certain that the LORD has spoken.
NET.21: How tragic that the once-faithful city has become a prostitute! She was once a center of justice, fairness resided in her, but now only murderers.
NET.22: Your silver has become scum, your beer is diluted with water.
NET.23: Your officials are rebels, they associate with thieves. All of them love bribery, and look for payoffs. They do not take up the cause of the orphan, or defend the rights of the widow.
NET.24: Therefore, the sovereign LORD who commands armies, the powerful ruler of Israel, says this: “Ah, I will seek vengeance against my adversaries, I will take revenge against my enemies.
NET.25: I will attack you; I will purify your metal with flux. I will remove all your slag.
NET.26: I will reestablish honest judges as in former times, wise advisers as in earlier days. Then you will be called, ‘The Just City, Faithful Town.’”
NET.27: Zion will be freed by justice, and her returnees by righteousness.
NET.28: All rebellious sinners will be shattered, those who abandon the LORD will perish.
NET.29: Indeed, they will be ashamed of the sacred trees you find so desirable; you will be embarrassed because of the sacred orchards where you choose to worship.
NET.30: For you will be like a tree whose leaves wither, like an orchard that is unwatered.
NET.31: The powerful will be like a thread of yarn, their deeds like a spark; both will burn together, and no one will put out the fire.
